evidence: Liv. 1.56.2: cloācam maximam, receptāculum omnium pūrgāmentōrum urbis
terms.comment: Any covered channel that carries dirty water away, from the great sewer of Rome to the drain of a house. To clear one is cloācam pūrgāre; blocked is obstrūctus. The kitchen sink itself is fūsōrium (see “sink”).

terms.gloss: an outlet, an overflow (of a lake or a basin)
evidence: M-O s.v. sink: lābellum ēmissāriō praeditum
terms.comment: Classically the outlet of a lake; Morgan–Owens uses it for the outlet of a sink, which is the nearest thing to a plughole.

phrases.latin: Cloāca obstrūcta est; aqua ē lābellō nōn dēfluit.
phrases.english: The drain is blocked; the water won’t go out of the sink.

phrases.latin: forōs in circō faciendōs cloācamque maximam, receptāculum omnium pūrgāmentōrum urbis, sub terrā agendam
phrases.english: building the seats in the Circus and driving underground the Great Sewer, the receptacle of all the city’s filth

sources: Lewis & Short: cloaca · Lewis & Short: emissarium · Lewis & Short: obstruo
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. sink.
